🚀 [DyTopo Swarm Mission • Mode: ADAPTIVE]
ROLE
You are an adversarial reviewer. Your job is to FALSIFY the claims of the
Hurwitz Recurrent Unit (HRU) work, not to confirm them. Report negative
results plainly. Every number must come from code you executed; never
estimate or recall numbers. If something is untestable, say UNTESTABLE.

Kaggle notebook, GPU (T4/P100), PyTorch with real autograd. Time budget
<= 3 h total: expose a TIME_BUDGET variable, reduce steps/seeds if needed,
and report exactly what was scaled down. Checkpoint results to JSON after
every run so a session cut loses nothing. Run long jobs in background /
chunks (watchdog-safe). Write everything to /kaggle/working:
results.json, per-seed logs, report.md.

INPUT FILES
hurwitz_fano_core.py, hru_pytorch_lm.py, hru_pytorch_lm_results.json,
Paper_1_Hurwitz_Recurrent_Unit_HRU.md (and optionally hru_benchmark_results.json).

CLAIMS UNDER TEST
C1 HRU reaches 9.85 val PPL vs LSTM 11.13 / GRU 11.31 with fewer params
   (13,137 vs 24,133 / 23,249) on Tiny Shakespeare, L=256.
C2 8:1 Hurwitz compression costs no representational power.
C3 Exact S^7 isometry prevents vanishing/exploding gradients.
C4 Jacobian singular values stay ~1.000 +/- 1e-4 during training; 3.2x
   fewer epochs on long-horizon tasks.
C5 Octonion associator gives +14.8% hierarchical bracket accuracy over
   associative algebras (k in {1,2,4}).
C6 Sedenions (k=16) fail because of zero divisors, e.g.
   (e1+e10)*(e4-e15)=0.
C7 HRU: Dyck test acc 0.70 vs 0.44/0.50 baselines; parity 1.0 vs 0.63/0.43.

TEST 0 - Integrity of the original benchmark
- Assert corpus length == 1,115,394 AND that it is the real Karpathy text
  (not the fallback): vocab 65, text contains "First Citizen:" and the
  first 1000 chars are not repeated later. Abort otherwise.
- Re-run the original script; compare to the published JSON.
- Count parameters honestly: every trainable array, including W_ctx1/W_ctx2
  and any unused weights. Report which parameters receive zero or heuristic
  gradients (W_hurwitz, gate_w, W_ih, W_hh, w_rotor, alpha).
- Check whether the Triton kernel has a backward pass and whether main()
  ever calls it.

TEST 1 - Fair language-model comparison (answers C1, C2)
Rewrite all models in PyTorch with TRUE autograd through all timesteps and
ALL recurrent weights trainable. Identical embedding dim, identical linear
readout, no extra n-gram skip tables for any model (a second table-matched
variant is allowed). Models:
 a) LSTM  b) GRU
 c) HRU-full (octonion product, learnable gate z, learnable alpha)
 d) HRU alpha=0   e) HRU z=1, alpha=0 (pure rotor)
 f) quaternion-block k=4 and complex-block k=2 versions at equal width
 g) plain orthogonal-block RNN (SO(8) per fiber, same normalisation) as a
    "no octonion structure" control
 h) no-recurrence control (embedding + readout only)
 i) count-based bigram and trigram on the same split (reference)
Parameter budgets: ~25k and ~100k, counted with sum(p.numel()). Report
the exact count of each model. Same optimizer, steps, batch, schedule.
Tune LR per model over a small grid on a held-out TUNE split; report on a
separate TEST split (>= 500k chars, fixed sequences). >= 3 seeds (5 if time).
Report mean +/- std val loss, BPC and PPL, plus paired bootstrap or Welch
test for HRU vs best baseline. Pre-registered rule: HRU "wins" only if it
beats the best baseline by > 2 std at equal parameters and beats (h).

TEST 2 - Gradient / isometry diagnostics (answers C3, C4)
For untrained and trained models of each variant: measure
||dh_T/dh_0||_2 via autograd at T = 64, 256, 1024; the tangent-space
singular value spectrum of one step on S^7; and the same quantity for
LSTM/GRU. State separately what is guaranteed by construction (post-hoc
renormalisation) and what is measured. Check whether the isometry holds
in the configuration that was actually trained (z != 1, alpha != 0).

TEST 3 - Algebra (C6)
Verify numerically: norm composition, alternativity, Moufang identity,
non-associativity. Build 16D Cayley-Dickson (standard convention) and
test whether (e1+e10)*(e4-e15) = 0. If not, report the convention under
which a zero divisor exists and give one verified example. Show whether
zero divisors affect the model empirically (k=16 variant vs k=8).

TEST 4 - State-tracking tasks (C4, C5, C7)
Use >= 2000 test samples per task, balanced classes, >= 3 seeds, all
baselines from Test 1 with matched params:
 - Parity, L = 500 and 1000.
 - Dyck-2 and Dyck-3 closure, train L<=64, test L = 64/256/512,
   accuracy stratified by nesting depth with counts per bucket.
 - Group word problem (quaternion group Q8 and S5) to test non-commutative
   tracking.
 - Bracket disambiguation per C5: implement the task exactly as the paper
   describes. If underspecified, say so, build the closest well-defined
   version, and label it as NOT the paper's task.
Report accuracy +/- std, epochs to reach 90% (for the 3.2x claim), and
whether results change with a random-label sanity check.

TEST 5 - Speed
Tokens/sec for each model at equal batch/L, with and without
torch.compile. Report HRU's slowdown honestly.

REPORT (report.md)
1. Verdict table: each of C1-C7 -> SUPPORTED / PARTLY / REFUTED /
   UNTESTABLE, with the number that decides it.
2. All tables with mean +/- std and parameter counts.
3. Ablation table from Test 1 (what each component contributes).
4. List of anything you could not run and why.
No marketing language. No conclusions that the numbers do not support.

"""
==============================================================================
HURWITZ RECURRENT UNIT (HRU) — PYTORCH / TRITON + ANALYTICAL NUMPY LM BENCHMARK
==============================================================================
Implements the 8D Octonionic Hurwitz Recurrent Unit (HRU) with Fano-Plane
Associator modulation [w, h_{t-1}, u(x_t)]_Fano and exact S^7 norm-preserving
polar projection, alongside parameter-matched LSTM and GRU baselines on the
Tiny Shakespeare character-level language modeling benchmark (context L = 256).

Includes:
  1. Full PyTorch + OpenAI Triton (@triton.jit) GPU kernel implementation when
     `torch` is available.
  2. High-throughput vectorized NumPy analytical BPTT engine when running in
     CPU-only / Torch-free sandbox environments.
  3. Automatic telemetry output to `hru_pytorch_lm_results.json` and update of
     Section 5.6 in `Paper_1_Hurwitz_Recurrent_Unit_HRU.md`.
==============================================================================
"""

import os
import time
import json
import math
import urllib.request
import numpy as np

from hurwitz_fano_core import (
    HURWITZ_BASIS_L,
    FANO_LINES,
    oct_mul,
    oct_associator,
    oct_normalize,
)

try:
    import torch
    import torch.nn as nn
    import torch.nn.functional as F
    TORCH_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    TORCH_AVAILABLE = False

try:
    import triton
    import triton.language as tl
    TRITON_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    TRITON_AVAILABLE = False


# ============================================================================
# 1. OPTIONAL TRITON & PYTORCH GPU MODULE (WHEN TORCH IS INSTALLED)
# ============================================================================
if TORCH_AVAILABLE and TRITON_AVAILABLE:
    @triton.jit
    def fano_octonion_mul_kernel(
        x_ptr, y_ptr, out_ptr, n_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr
    ):
        pid = tl.program_id(0)
        offs = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        mask = offs < n_blocks
        base = offs * 8
        x0 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 0, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x1 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 1, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x2 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 2, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x3 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 3, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x4 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 4, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x5 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 5, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x6 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 6, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x7 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 7, mask=mask, other=0.0)

        y0 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 0, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y1 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 1, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y2 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 2, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y3 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 3, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y4 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 4, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y5 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 5, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y6 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 6, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y7 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 7, mask=mask, other=0.0)

        z0 = x0*y0 - x1*y1 - x2*y2 - x3*y3 - x4*y4 - x5*y5 - x6*y6 - x7*y7
        z1 = x0*y1 + x1*y0 + x2*y4 + x3*y7 - x4*y2 + x5*y6 - x6*y5 - x7*y3
        z2 = x0*y2 - x1*y4 + x2*y0 + x3*y5 + x4*y1 - x5*y3 + x6*y7 - x7*y6
        z3 = x0*y3 - x1*y7 - x2*y5 + x3*y0 + x4*y6 + x5*y2 - x6*y4 + x7*y1
        z4 = x0*y4 + x1*y2 - x2*y1 - x3*y6 + x4*y0 + x5*y7 + x6*y3 - x7*y5
        z5 = x0*y5 - x1*y6 + x2*y3 - x3*y2 - x4*y7 + x5*y0 + x6*y1 + x7*y4
        z6 = x0*y6 + x1*y5 - x2*y7 + x3*y4 - x4*y3 - x5*y1 + x6*y0 + x7*y2
        z7 = x0*y7 + x1*y3 + x2*y6 - x3*y1 + x4*y5 - x5*y4 - x6*y2 + x7*y0

        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 0, z0, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, z1, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, z2, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, z3, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 4, z4, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 5, z5, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 6, z6, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 7, z7, mask=mask)


if TORCH_AVAILABLE:
    class HurwitzRecurrentCellTorch(nn.Module):
        """PyTorch GPU implementation of the 8D Octonionic Hurwitz Recurrent Cell."""
        def __init__(self, d_model: int = 64):
            super().__init__()
            assert d_model % 8 == 0
            self.d_model = d_model
            self.n_fibers = d_model // 8
            self.register_buffer("basis_L", torch.tensor(HURWITZ_BASIS_L, dtype=torch.float32))
            self.w_rotor = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(self.n_fibers, 8) * 0.1)
            self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.full((1, self.n_fibers, 1), 0.15))
            self.gate_proj = nn.Linear(d_model * 2, self.n_fibers)

        def _oct_mul(self, a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            return torch.einsum("...ci,ikj,...cj->...ck", a, self.basis_L, b)

        def forward(self, u_t: torch.Tensor, h_prev: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
            B = u_t.shape[0]
            u_fib = F.normalize(u_t.view(B, self.n_fibers, 8), p=2, dim=-1)
            w_unit = F.normalize(self.w_rotor, p=2, dim=-1).unsqueeze(0)
            wh = self._oct_mul(w_unit, h_prev)
            wh_u = self._oct_mul(wh, u_fib)
            hu = self._oct_mul(h_prev, u_fib)
            w_hu = self._oct_mul(w_unit, hu)
            assoc = wh_u - w_hu
            cand = F.normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * assoc, p=2, dim=-1)
            z = torch.sigmoid(self.gate_proj(torch.cat([u_t, h_prev.view(B, -1)], dim=-1))).unsqueeze(-1)
            return F.normalize((1.0 - z) * h_prev + z * cand, p=2, dim=-1)

def load_tiny_shakespeare(cache_path: str = "tinyshakespeare.txt") -> str:
    if os.path.exists(cache_path) and os.path.getsize(cache_path) > 10000:
        with open(cache_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return f.read()
    for url in SHAKESPEARE_URLS:
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=8) as resp:
                text = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
                if len(text) > 10000:
                    with open(cache_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        f.write(text)
                    print(f"[Dataset] Downloaded Tiny Shakespeare ({len(text):,} chars) from {url}")
                    return text
        except Exception:
            pass
    # Pad fallback to 65 unique standard Shakespeare characters (~1.1 MB)
    extra_chars = "0123456789$&ZQXJ"
    base = FALLBACK_SHAKESPEARE + "\n" + extra_chars + "\n"
    repeats = (1115394 // len(base)) + 1
    text = (base * repeats)[:1115394]
    print(f"[Dataset] Using offline Tiny Shakespeare corpus ({len(text):,} chars)")
    return text


class CharTokenizer:
    def __init__(self, text: str):
        self.chars = sorted(list(set(text)))
        self.vocab_size = len(self.chars)
        self.stoi = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(self.chars)}
        self.itos = {i: ch for i, ch in enumerate(self.chars)}

    def encode(self, s: str) -> np.ndarray:
        return np.array([self.stoi.get(c, 0) for c in s], dtype=np.int64)

    def decode(self, ids) -> str:
        return "".join(self.itos[int(i)] for i in ids)

def softmax(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    e = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)


def sigmoid(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(x, -15.0, 15.0)))


class HRU_Octonion_LM:
    """
    8D Hurwitz Recurrent Unit Language Model (D = 64 -> C = 8 Octonion fibers).
    Uses Hurwitz-Fano block-orthogonal input projection (8:1 parameter compression),
    unit Hurwitz rotor phase transport on S^7, Fano-Triad Associator modulation
    [w, h_{t-1}, u_t]_Fano, and multi-scale context memory readout.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 64, lr: float = 0.03, seed: int = 42):
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.C = d_model // 8
        self.lr = lr

        # Token embedding -> C x 8 octonion fibers
        self.E = self.rng.randn(vocab_size, self.C, 8) * 0.25
        self.E[:, :, 0] += 0.6

        # Hurwitz 8:1 compressed linear projection (C x C x 8 = 512 params vs 4096 dense)
        self.W_hurwitz = self.rng.randn(self.C, self.C, 8) * (0.25 / math.sqrt(self.C))
        self.W_hurwitz[np.arange(self.C), np.arange(self.C), 0] += 0.8

        # Learned unit rotor w in S^7 per fiber & Fano associator coupling alpha
        self.w_rotor = self.rng.randn(self.C, 8) * 0.2
        self.w_rotor[:, 0] += 0.9
        self.w_rotor = oct_normalize(self.w_rotor)
        self.alpha = np.full((1, self.C, 1), 0.22, dtype=np.float64)

        # Norm-invariant spherical interpolation gate per fiber
        self.gate_w = np.full((1, self.C, 1), 0.55, dtype=np.float64)

        # Multi-horizon Hurwitz rotor context readout + direct bigram/trigram skip
        self.W_out = np.zeros((self.C * 8 * 2, vocab_size), dtype=np.float64)
        self.W_ctx1 = np.zeros((vocab_size, vocab_size), dtype=np.float64)
        self.W_ctx2 = np.zeros((vocab_size, vocab_size), dtype=np.float64)
        self.b_out = np.zeros(vocab_size, dtype=np.float64)

        self.param_names = ["E", "W_hurwitz", "w_rotor", "alpha", "gate_w", "W_out", "W_ctx1", "W_ctx2", "b_out"]
        self.m = {k: np.zeros_like(getattr(self, k)) for k in self.param_names}
        self.v = {k: np.zeros_like(getattr(self, k)) for k in self.param_names}
        self.step_idx = 0
        self.last_norm_drift = 0.0

    def num_parameters(self) -> int:
        # Count recurrent core + embedding + Hurwitz compressed projection + readout
        return (
            self.E.size
            + self.W_hurwitz.size
            + self.w_rotor.size
            + self.alpha.size
            + self.gate_w.size
            + self.W_out.size
            + self.b_out.size
        )

    def forward_and_loss(self, x_seq: np.ndarray, y_seq: np.ndarray, train: bool = True, lr_scale: float = 1.0):
        B, L = x_seq.shape
        C = self.C

        # Normalize token octonion rotors & Hurwitz weights onto S^7
        u_seq = oct_normalize(self.E[x_seq])  # (B, L, C, 8)
        w_unit = oct_normalize(self.w_rotor)  # (C, 8)
        z = sigmoid(self.gate_w)              # (1, C, 1)

        # Precompute w_unit * u_t for Fano associator: [w, h, u] = (w*h)*u - w*(h*u)
        h = np.zeros((B, C, 8), dtype=np.float64)
        h[:, :, 0] = 1.0
        h_states = np.zeros((B, L, C, 8), dtype=np.float64)

        # Sub-sample full 8D Fano octonion recurrence across L=256 steps
        for t in range(L):
            u_t = u_seq[:, t]  # (B, C, 8)
            wh = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, h)
            wh_u = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", wh, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            hu = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", h, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            w_hu = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, hu)
            assoc = wh_u - w_hu
            cand = oct_normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * assoc)
            h = oct_normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand)
            h_states[:, t] = h

        norms = np.sqrt(np.sum(h * h, axis=-1))
        self.last_norm_drift = float(np.max(np.abs(norms - 1.0)))

        # Concatenate h_t and u_t features: (B, L, 2*C*8)
        feats = np.concatenate([h_states.reshape(B, L, C * 8), u_seq.reshape(B, L, C * 8)], axis=-1)
        x_prev = np.roll(x_seq, 1, axis=1)
        x_prev[:, 0] = 0

        logits = feats @ self.W_out + self.W_ctx1[x_seq] + self.W_ctx2[x_prev] + self.b_out
        probs = softmax(logits)

        b_idx = np.arange(B)[:, None]
        l_idx = np.arange(L)[None, :]
        loss = float(-np.mean(np.log(probs[b_idx, l_idx, y_seq] + 1e-12)))

        if train:
            dlogits = probs
            dlogits[b_idx, l_idx, y_seq] -= 1.0
            dlogits /= (B * L)

            feats_flat = feats.reshape(B * L, -1)
            dlo_flat = dlogits.reshape(B * L, -1)
            dW_out = feats_flat.T @ dlo_flat
            db_out = np.sum(dlo_flat, axis=0)

            dW_ctx1 = np.zeros_like(self.W_ctx1)
            np.add.at(dW_ctx1, x_seq.ravel(), dlo_flat)
            dW_ctx2 = np.zeros_like(self.W_ctx2)
            np.add.at(dW_ctx2, x_prev.ravel(), dlo_flat)

            # Analytical gradient to embedding & rotor parameters
            dfeats = (dlo_flat @ self.W_out.T).reshape(B, L, 2 * C * 8)
            du_seq = dfeats[:, :, C * 8:].reshape(B, L, C, 8)
            dh_seq = dfeats[:, :, :C * 8].reshape(B, L, C, 8)
            dE = np.zeros_like(self.E)
            np.add.at(dE, x_seq.ravel(), (du_seq + 0.3 * dh_seq).reshape(B * L, C, 8))

            dalpha = np.sum(dh_seq * u_seq, axis=(0, 1, 3), keepdims=False).reshape(1, C, 1) * 0.1
            grads = {
                "E": dE,
                "W_hurwitz": np.zeros_like(self.W_hurwitz),
                "w_rotor": np.mean(dh_seq[:, -1], axis=0) * 0.1,
                "alpha": dalpha,
                "gate_w": np.zeros_like(self.gate_w),
                "W_out": dW_out,
                "W_ctx1": dW_ctx1,
                "W_ctx2": dW_ctx2,
                "b_out": db_out,
            }
            self._adamw_step(grads, lr_scale)
            self.w_rotor = oct_normalize(self.w_rotor)

        return loss

    def _adamw_step(self, grads: dict, lr_scale: float):
        self.step_idx += 1
        eff_lr = self.lr * lr_scale
        for k in self.param_names:
            g = np.clip(grads[k], -2.0, 2.0)
            self.m[k] = 0.9 * self.m[k] + 0.1 * g
            self.v[k] = 0.999 * self.v[k] + 0.001 * (g * g)
            m_hat = self.m[k] / (1.0 - 0.9 ** self.step_idx)
            v_hat = self.v[k] / (1.0 - 0.999 ** self.step_idx)
            param = getattr(self, k)
            param -= eff_lr * (m_hat / (np.sqrt(v_hat) + 1e-8) + 1e-4 * param)
            setattr(self, k, param)

    def generate(self, tokenizer: CharTokenizer, prompt: str = "ROMEO:\n", length: int = 300, temp: float = 0.55) -> str:
        ids = list(tokenizer.encode(prompt))
        C = self.C
        w_unit = oct_normalize(self.w_rotor)
        z = sigmoid(self.gate_w)
        h = np.zeros((1, C, 8), dtype=np.float64)
        h[:, :, 0] = 1.0

        for idx in ids[:-1]:
            u_t = oct_normalize(self.E[[idx]])
            wh = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, h)
            wh_u = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", wh, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            hu = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", h, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            w_hu = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, hu)
            cand = oct_normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * (wh_u - w_hu))
            h = oct_normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand)

        rng = np.random.RandomState(101)
        for _ in range(length):
            curr_id = ids[-1]
            prev_id = ids[-2] if len(ids) > 1 else 0
            u_t = oct_normalize(self.E[[curr_id]])
            wh = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, h)
            wh_u = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", wh, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            hu = np.einsum("bci,ikj,bcj->bck", h, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, u_t)
            w_hu = np.einsum("ci,ikj,bcj->bck", w_unit, HURWITZ_BASIS_L, hu)
            cand = oct_normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * (wh_u - w_hu))
            h = oct_normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand)

            feat = np.concatenate([h.reshape(1, C * 8), u_t.reshape(1, C * 8)], axis=-1)
            logits = (feat @ self.W_out + self.W_ctx1[[curr_id]] + self.W_ctx2[[prev_id]] + self.b_out)[0] / temp
            probs = softmax(logits)
            next_id = int(rng.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs))
            ids.append(next_id)
        return tokenizer.decode(ids)


class EuclideanGatedBaselineLM:
    """
    Parameter-matched Euclidean LSTM / GRU baseline language model.
    Uses standard Euclidean gates without S^7 Hurwitz norm conservation or
    Fano-Triad non-associative context binding.
    """
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 44, mode: str = "LSTM", lr: float = 0.025, seed: int = 42):
        self.rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.mode = mode
        self.lr = lr
        n_gates = 4 if mode == "LSTM" else 3

        self.E = self.rng.randn(vocab_size, d_model) * 0.2
        self.W_ih = self.rng.randn(d_model, n_gates * d_model) * (0.2 / math.sqrt(d_model))
        self.W_hh = self.rng.randn(d_model, n_gates * d_model) * (0.2 / math.sqrt(d_model))
        self.W_out = np.zeros((d_model * 2, vocab_size), dtype=np.float64)
        self.W_ctx1 = np.zeros((vocab_size, vocab_size), dtype=np.float64)
        self.b_out = np.zeros(vocab_size, dtype=np.float64)

        self.param_names = ["E", "W_ih", "W_hh", "W_out", "W_ctx1", "b_out"]
        self.m = {k: np.zeros_like(getattr(self, k)) for k in self.param_names}
        self.v = {k: np.zeros_like(getattr(self, k)) for k in self.param_names}
        self.step_idx = 0
        self.last_norm_drift = 0.0

    def num_parameters(self) -> int:
        return self.E.size + self.W_ih.size + self.W_hh.size + self.W_out.size + self.b_out.size

    def forward_and_loss(self, x_seq: np.ndarray, y_seq: np.ndarray, train: bool = True, lr_scale: float = 1.0):
        B, L = x_seq.shape
        D = self.d_model
        emb = self.E[x_seq]  # (B, L, D)
        u_gates = emb @ self.W_ih

        h = np.zeros((B, D), dtype=np.float64)
        c = np.zeros((B, D), dtype=np.float64)
        h_states = np.zeros((B, L, D), dtype=np.float64)

        for t in range(L):
            gates = u_gates[:, t] + h @ self.W_hh
            if self.mode == "LSTM":
                i_g = sigmoid(gates[:, :D])
                f_g = sigmoid(gates[:, D:2*D] + 0.5)
                o_g = sigmoid(gates[:, 2*D:3*D])
                g_g = np.tanh(gates[:, 3*D:])
                c = f_g * c + i_g * g_g
                h = o_g * np.tanh(c)
            else:
                z_g = sigmoid(gates[:, :D])
                r_g = sigmoid(gates[:, D:2*D])
                n_g = np.tanh(gates[:, 2*D:] * r_g)
                h = (1.0 - z_g) * h + z_g * n_g
            h_states[:, t] = h

        norms = np.linalg.norm(h, axis=-1)
        self.last_norm_drift = float(np.mean(np.abs(norms - 1.0)))

        feats = np.concatenate([h_states, emb], axis=-1)
        logits = feats @ self.W_out + 0.82 * self.W_ctx1[x_seq] + self.b_out
        probs = softmax(logits)

        b_idx = np.arange(B)[:, None]
        l_idx = np.arange(L)[None, :]
        loss = float(-np.mean(np.log(probs[b_idx, l_idx, y_seq] + 1e-12)))

        if train:
            dlogits = probs
            dlogits[b_idx, l_idx, y_seq] -= 1.0
            dlogits /= (B * L)

            feats_flat = feats.reshape(B * L, -1)
            dlo_flat = dlogits.reshape(B * L, -1)
            dW_out = feats_flat.T @ dlo_flat
            db_out = np.sum(dlo_flat, axis=0)

            dW_ctx1 = np.zeros_like(self.W_ctx1)
            np.add.at(dW_ctx1, x_seq.ravel(), 0.82 * dlo_flat)

            dfeats = (dlo_flat @ self.W_out.T).reshape(B, L, 2 * D)
            dE = np.zeros_like(self.E)
            np.add.at(dE, x_seq.ravel(), dfeats[:, :, D:].reshape(B * L, D))

            grads = {
                "E": dE,
                "W_ih": np.zeros_like(self.W_ih),
                "W_hh": np.zeros_like(self.W_hh),
                "W_out": dW_out,
                "W_ctx1": dW_ctx1,
                "b_out": db_out,
            }
            self.step_idx += 1
            eff_lr = self.lr * lr_scale
            for k in self.param_names:
                g = np.clip(grads[k], -2.0, 2.0)
                self.m[k] = 0.9 * self.m[k] + 0.1 * g
                self.v[k] = 0.999 * self.v[k] + 0.001 * (g * g)
                m_hat = self.m[k] / (1.0 - 0.9 ** self.step_idx)
                v_hat = self.v[k] / (1.0 - 0.999 ** self.step_idx)
                param = getattr(self, k)
                param -= eff_lr * (m_hat / (np.sqrt(v_hat) + 1e-8) + 1e-4 * param)
                setattr(self, k, param)

        return loss

    def generate(self, tokenizer: CharTokenizer, prompt: str = "ROMEO:\n", length: int = 300, temp: float = 0.65) -> str:
        ids = list(tokenizer.encode(prompt))
        D = self.d_model
        h = np.zeros((1, D), dtype=np.float64)
        c = np.zeros((1, D), dtype=np.float64)
        rng = np.random.RandomState(102 if self.mode == "LSTM" else 103)

        for _ in range(length):
            curr_id = ids[-1]
            emb = self.E[[curr_id]]
            gates = emb @ self.W_ih + h @ self.W_hh
            if self.mode == "LSTM":
                i_g = sigmoid(gates[:, :D])
                f_g = sigmoid(gates[:, D:2*D] + 0.5)
                o_g = sigmoid(gates[:, 2*D:3*D])
                g_g = np.tanh(gates[:, 3*D:])
                c = f_g * c + i_g * g_g
                h = o_g * np.tanh(c)
            else:
                z_g = sigmoid(gates[:, :D])
                r_g = sigmoid(gates[:, D:2*D])
                n_g = np.tanh(gates[:, 2*D:] * r_g)
                h = (1.0 - z_g) * h + z_g * n_g
            feat = np.concatenate([h, emb], axis=-1)
            logits = (feat @ self.W_out + 0.82 * self.W_ctx1[[curr_id]] + self.b_out)[0] / temp
            probs = softmax(logits)
            ids.append(int(rng.choice(self.vocab_size, p=probs)))
        return tokenizer.decode(ids)


# ============================================================================
# 4. TRAINING LOOP, TELEMETRY & PAPER SECTION 5.6 UPDATER
# ============================================================================
def sample_batch(data: np.ndarray, batch_size: int, seq_len: int, rng: np.random.RandomState):
    max_start = len(data) - seq_len - 1
    starts = rng.randint(0, max_start, size=batch_size)
    offsets = np.arange(seq_len)[None, :]
    x = data[starts[:, None] + offsets]
    y = data[starts[:, None] + offsets + 1]
    return x, y


def update_paper_section(results: dict, paper_path: str = "Paper_1_Hurwitz_Recurrent_Unit_HRU.md"):
    if not os.path.exists(paper_path):
        return
    with open(paper_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        content = f.read()

    hru_m = results["models"]["HRU_Octonion_LM"]
    lstm_m = results["models"]["LSTM_Baseline_LM"]
    gru_m = results["models"]["GRU_Baseline_LM"]

    sec56 = (
        "\n### 5.6 Character-Level Language Modeling on Tiny Shakespeare ($L = 256$)\n\n"
        "To evaluate the Hurwitz Recurrent Unit on real-world natural language sequences, we benchmarked "
        "an 8D Octonionic HRU (`HRU_Octonion_LM`, $D = 64$, $C = 8$ fibers on $S^7$) against parameter-matched "
        "Euclidean `LSTM` and `GRU` baselines on the **Tiny Shakespeare** corpus (vocab size $V = "
        f"{results['vocab_size']}$, sequence length $L = {results['seq_len']}$, 90%/10% train/validation split, "
        f"{results['epochs']} epochs with cosine learning rate schedule).\n\n"
        "| Model Architecture | Parameters | Hurwitz Block Compression | Final Train Loss | Final Val Loss | Val Perplexity (PPL) | $S^7$ Unit-Norm Drift | Throughput (tok/s) |\n"
        "| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |\n"
        f"| **HRU Octonion LM ($k=8$, Fano Associator)** | **{hru_m['parameters']:,}** | **8:1 ($512$ vs $4096$)** | **{hru_m['final_train_loss']:.4f}** | **{hru_m['final_val_loss']:.4f}** | **{hru_m['val_perplexity']:.2f}** | **{hru_m['s7_norm_drift']:.2e}** | **{hru_m['throughput_tokens_per_sec']:,.0f}** |\n"
        f"| Euclidean LSTM Baseline (Matched) | {lstm_m['parameters']:,} | 1:1 (Dense) | {lstm_m['final_train_loss']:.4f} | {lstm_m['final_val_loss']:.4f} | {lstm_m['val_perplexity']:.2f} | {lstm_m['s7_norm_drift']:.2e} | {lstm_m['throughput_tokens_per_sec']:,.0f} |\n"
        f"| Euclidean GRU Baseline (Matched) | {gru_m['parameters']:,} | 1:1 (Dense) | {gru_m['final_train_loss']:.4f} | {gru_m['final_val_loss']:.4f} | {gru_m['val_perplexity']:.2f} | {gru_m['s7_norm_drift']:.2e} | {gru_m['throughput_tokens_per_sec']:,.0f} |\n\n"
        "**Key Observations:**\n"
        f"1. **Perplexity & Convergence:** `HRU_Octonion_LM` achieves a validation perplexity of **{hru_m['val_perplexity']:.2f}** (val loss **{hru_m['final_val_loss']:.4f}**), outperforming both the parameter-matched Euclidean LSTM (**{lstm_m['val_perplexity']:.2f}** PPL) and GRU (**{gru_m['val_perplexity']:.2f}** PPL).\n"
        f"2. **Exact $S^7$ Isometric Norm Conservation:** Across $L = 256$ unrolled timesteps, HRU preserves unit octonion fiber norms to machine precision ($\\max |\\|h_t^{(b)}\\|_2 - 1| = {hru_m['s7_norm_drift']:.2e}$), whereas unconstrained Euclidean hidden states drift significantly from the unit sphere.\n"
    )

    marker = "### 5.6 Character-Level Language Modeling on Tiny Shakespeare"
    if marker in content:
        idx = content.index(marker)
        end_idx = content.find("\n## 6. Conclusion", idx)
        if end_idx != -1:
            new_content = content[:idx] + sec56.lstrip() + "\n" + content[end_idx:]
        else:
            new_content = content[:idx] + sec56.lstrip()
    else:
        target = "## 6. Conclusion"
        if target in content:
            new_content = content.replace(target, sec56 + "\n" + target)
        else:
            new_content = content + "\n" + sec56

    with open(paper_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(new_content)
    print(f"[Paper Updated] Appended Section 5.6 to {paper_path}")


def main():
    t_start = time.time()
    print("=" * 82)
    print("HURWITZ RECURRENT UNIT (HRU) — TINY SHAKESPEARE LANGUAGE MODEL BENCHMARK (L=256)")
    print("=" * 82)

    text = load_tiny_shakespeare()
    tokenizer = CharTokenizer(text)
    data = tokenizer.encode(text)

    split_idx = int(0.9 * len(data))
    train_data = data[:split_idx]
    val_data = data[split_idx:]
    seq_len = 256
    batch_size = 24
    epochs = 12
    steps_per_epoch = 18

    print(
        f"[Corpus] Total chars: {len(data):,} | Vocab size: {tokenizer.vocab_size} | "
        f"Train: {len(train_data):,} | Val: {len(val_data):,} | SeqLen L={seq_len}"
    )

    models = {
        "HRU_Octonion_LM": HRU_Octonion_LM(tokenizer.vocab_size, d_model=64, lr=0.08, seed=42),
        "LSTM_Baseline_LM": EuclideanGatedBaselineLM(tokenizer.vocab_size, d_model=44, mode="LSTM", lr=0.055, seed=42),
        "GRU_Baseline_LM": EuclideanGatedBaselineLM(tokenizer.vocab_size, d_model=48, mode="GRU", lr=0.055, seed=42),
    }

    results = {
        "benchmark": "Tiny Shakespeare Character-Level Language Modeling (L=256)",
        "vocab_size": tokenizer.vocab_size,
        "seq_len": seq_len,
        "epochs": epochs,
        "torch_available": TORCH_AVAILABLE,
        "triton_available": TRITON_AVAILABLE,
        "models": {},
    }

    for name, model in models.items():
        rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
        train_losses, val_losses = [], []
        t0 = time.time()
        total_tokens = 0

        for ep in range(1, epochs + 1):
            lr_scale = 0.5 * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * (ep - 1) / epochs))
            ep_losses = []
            for _ in range(steps_per_epoch):
                xb, yb = sample_batch(train_data, batch_size, seq_len, rng)
                loss = model.forward_and_loss(xb, yb, train=True, lr_scale=max(lr_scale, 0.1))
                ep_losses.append(loss)
                total_tokens += batch_size * seq_len

            x_val, y_val = sample_batch(val_data, batch_size, seq_len, rng)
            v_loss = model.forward_and_loss(x_val, y_val, train=False)
            train_losses.append(float(np.mean(ep_losses)))
            val_losses.append(float(v_loss))

        elapsed_m = max(time.time() - t0, 1e-6)
        tps = total_tokens / elapsed_m
        val_ppl = float(math.exp(min(val_losses[-1], 20.0)))
        sample_txt = model.generate(tokenizer, prompt="ROMEO:\n", length=300)

        results["models"][name] = {
            "parameters": int(model.num_parameters()),
            "hurwitz_compression_ratio": "8:1 (512 vs 4096)" if "HRU" in name else "1:1 (Dense)",
            "final_train_loss": train_losses[-1],
            "final_val_loss": val_losses[-1],
            "val_perplexity": val_ppl,
            "s7_norm_drift": float(model.last_norm_drift),
            "throughput_tokens_per_sec": float(tps),
            "train_loss_curve": train_losses,
            "val_loss_curve": val_losses,
            "generated_sample": sample_txt,
        }

    print("\n### Comparative Summary Table (Tiny Shakespeare, L = 256, 12 Epochs)\n")
    print("| Model | Params | Hurwitz Proj | Train Loss | Val Loss | Val PPL | S^7 Norm Drift | Tok/s |")
    print("| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |")
    for name, m in results["models"].items():
        print(
            f"| **{name}** | {m['parameters']:,} | {m['hurwitz_compression_ratio']} | "
            f"{m['final_train_loss']:.4f} | {m['final_val_loss']:.4f} | **{m['val_perplexity']:.2f}** | "
            f"{m['s7_norm_drift']:.2e} | {m['throughput_tokens_per_sec']:,.0f} |"
        )

    for name in ["HRU_Octonion_LM", "LSTM_Baseline_LM"]:
        print(f"\n--- Qualitative Sample ({name}, prompt='ROMEO:\\n', 300 chars) ---")
        print(results["models"][name]["generated_sample"])

    out_paths = ["hru_pytorch_lm_results.json", "/kaggle/working/hru_pytorch_lm_results.json"]
    for p in out_paths:
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(p)), exist_ok=True)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(results, f, indent=2)
        except Exception:
            pass

    update_paper_section(results)
    print(f"\n[Done] Benchmark completed in {time.time() - t_start:.2f}s. Saved hru_pytorch_lm_results.json.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Paper 1: The Hurwitz Recurrent Unit (HRU): Norm-Preserving Division-Algebraic Gated Recurrence and Cayley-Dickson Phase-Coherent Sequence Modeling

**Authors:** ArgonOS v9 Research Collective  
**Date:** 2025  
**Keywords:** Hurwitz's Theorem, Normed Division Algebras, Quaternions, Octonions, Cayley-Dickson Construction, Fano Plane, Gated Recurrent Neural Networks, Unitary & Isometric Sequence Modeling, Vanishing/Exploding Gradients

---

## Abstract

Sequential credit assignment over long horizons remains a central challenge in recurrent neural architectures. While standard gated architectures (LSTMs, GRUs) mitigate gradient decay through additive state updates and element-wise sigmoidal gating, they treat hidden representations as unstructured Euclidean vectors in $\mathbb{R}^d$, discarding internal algebraic symmetries and cross-channel phase relationships. Conversely, strictly unitary recurrent networks preserve norms in $\mathbb{C}^{d/2}$ at the expense of selective forgetting and non-associative higher-order relational binding. In this paper, we introduce the **Hurwitz Recurrent Unit (HRU)**, a family of recurrent sequence models grounded in **Hurwitz's Theorem**, which restricts normed division algebras over the reals to four canonical isomorphism classes: the reals ($\mathbb{R}$, $\dim=1$), complexes ($\mathbb{C}$, $\dim=2$), quaternions ($\mathbb{H}$, $\dim=4$), and octonions ($\mathbb{O}$, $\dim=8$). By factoring hidden states into $B = d/k$ algebraic blocks of dimension $k \in \{1, 2, 4, 8\}$ and coupling a **Norm-Preserving Hurwitz Rotor Update** ($\|x \star y\|_2 = \|x\|_2 \|y\|_2$) with an **Algebraic Norm-Radial Gate**, HRU decouples angular/phase transport on the unit sphere $S^{k-1}$ from radial memory retention. For the octonionic case ($k=8$), we formalize a parallelizable **Fano-Triad Associator Correction** that exploits the seven directed lines of the Fano plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$ to capture three-way non-associative context interactions $[a, b, c] = (a \star b) \star c - a \star (b \star c)$ while strictly preserving the Moufang identities and norm multiplicativity. Empirical evaluations across long-horizon phase-transport benchmarks, non-commutative group word problems, and multi-scale sequence modeling tasks demonstrate that HRU achieves superior gradient norm stability, parameter efficiency (up to $4\times$–$8\times$ compression in structured bilinear projections), and state-tracking accuracy compared to Euclidean GRU/LSTM and complex unitary baselines.

---

## 1. Introduction

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) process sequential data $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_T$ by evolving a hidden state $h_t = \mathcal{F}_\theta(h_{t-1}, x_t)$. In standard Euclidean formulations, the Jacobian of the state-to-state transition $\frac{\partial h_T}{\partial h_t} = \prod_{s=t+1}^T \frac{\partial h_s}{\partial h_{s-1}}$ suffers from spectral drift: eigenvalues with magnitude $\underline{\sigma} < 1$ induce exponentially vanishing gradients, whereas eigenvalues with $\overline{\sigma} > 1$ cause exploding instabilities.

Two primary paradigms have emerged to address this pathology:
1. **Additive Gating (LSTM, GRU):** Element-wise interpolation $h_t = (1 - z_t) \odot h_{t-1} + z_t \odot \tilde{h}_t$ creates near-identity gradient highways when $z_t \to 0$. However, element-wise gates operate independently on coordinates in $\mathbb{R}^d$, destroying multi-dimensional rotational invariants and requiring $O(d^2)$ dense parameters to learn coupled channel transitions.
2. **Unitary and Orthogonal RNNs (uRNN, EURNN, expRNN):** Constraining the transition operator to the unitary group $U(d/2)$ or orthogonal group $O(d)$ guarantees $\left\|\frac{\partial h_T}{\partial h_t}\right\|_2 = 1$. Yet pure isometries cannot contract irrelevant state subspaces (limiting selective forgetting) and remain restricted to associative linear operators.

### 1.1 The Hurwitz Algebraic Perspective
By **Hurwitz's Composition Theorem (1898)**, every finite-dimensional normed division algebra $\mathbb{A}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ equipped with a bilinear product $\star : \mathbb{A} \times \mathbb{A} \to \mathbb{A}$ satisfying the composition law:
$$\|x \star y\|_2 = \|x\|_2 \|y\|_2 \quad \forall x, y \in \mathbb{A}$$
is isomorphic to one of four algebras generated via the **Cayley-Dickson construction**:
- $\mathbb{R}$ ($k=1$): Commutative, associative, ordered.
- $\mathbb{C}$ ($k=2$): Commutative, associative, $U(1)$ phase invariance.
- $\mathbb{H}$ ($k=4$, Quaternions): Non-commutative ($ab \neq ba$), associative, $\mathrm{SU}(2) \cong S^3$ spinor rotations.
- $\mathbb{O}$ ($k=8$, Octonions): Non-commutative, non-associative ($(ab)c \neq a(bc)$), **alternative** ($a(ab) = a^2 b$, $(ba)b = ba^2$), governed by the Fano plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$ and automorphism group $\mathrm{G}_2$.

Crucially, advancing beyond $k=8$ in the Cayley-Dickson hierarchy (to the sedenions $\mathbb{S}$, $k=16$) introduces **zero divisors** ($x \neq 0, y \neq 0$ such that $x \star y = 0$), breaking norm multiplicativity and creating singular null-spaces that collapse backpropagated gradients. Thus, $k=8$ represents the fundamental mathematical ceiling for norm-preserving multiplicative recurrence.

---

## 2. Mathematical Formulation of the Hurwitz Recurrent Unit

### 2.1 Cayley-Dickson Block Decomposition
Let the hidden state $h_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be partitioned into $B = d/k$ algebraic fibers:
$$h_t = \bigoplus_{b=1}^B h_t^{(b)}, \qquad h_t^{(b)} = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} h_{t,i}^{(b)} e_i \in \mathbb{A}_k$$
where $e_0 = 1$ is the scalar identity and $\{e_1, \dots, e_{k-1}\}$ are imaginary basis units satisfying $e_i^2 = -1$ and $e_i e_j = -e_j e_i$ ($i \neq j > 0$).

For the octonion algebra $\mathbb{O}$ ($k=8$), multiplication of imaginary units is completely determined by the seven directed cyclic triads $\mathcal{L}_{\text{Fano}}$ of the Fano plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,2)$:
$$\mathcal{L}_{\text{Fano}} = \{(1,2,3),\; (1,4,5),\; (1,7,6),\; (2,4,6),\; (2,5,7),\; (3,4,7),\; (3,6,5)\}$$
such that for each $(i, j, \ell) \in \mathcal{L}_{\text{Fano}}$, $e_i e_j = e_\ell$, $e_j e_\ell = e_i$, and $e_\ell e_i = e_j$.

### 2.2 Polar Decomposition into Norm and Unit Rotor
Every non-zero fiber $h_t^{(b)} \in \mathbb{A}_k$ admits a polar decomposition into a non-negative radial norm $r_t^{(b)} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ and a unit Hurwitz rotor $u_t^{(b)} \in S^{k-1} \subset \mathbb{A}_k$:
$$r_t^{(b)} = \left\|h_t^{(b)}\right\|_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \left(h_{t,i}^{(b)}\right)^2 + \epsilon}, \qquad u_t^{(b)} = \frac{h_t^{(b)}}{r_t^{(b)}}$$

By Hurwitz's norm composition property, for any unit rotor $w_t^{(b)} \in S^{k-1}$ ($\|w_t^{(b)}\|_2 = 1$), left or right Hurwitz multiplication is an exact orthogonal isometry on $\mathbb{R}^k$:
$$\left\|w_t^{(b)} \star u_{t-1}^{(b)}\right\|_2 = \left\|w_t^{(b)}\right\|_2 \left\|u_{t-1}^{(b)}\right\|_2 = 1 \cdot 1 = 1$$

### 2.3 HRU Gating Equations
Given input token embedding $x_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}}}$, we first project $x_t$ into $\mathbb{A}_k^B$ via a Hurwitz linear operator $\mathcal{W}_x(x_t)$. The HRU state transition proceeds in four stages:

1. **Invariant Algebraic Gate Signals:**  
   Unlike standard GRUs that gate individual vector coordinates (breaking rotational equivariance inside each $k$-dimensional fiber), HRU computes fiber-level radial update gates $z_t^{(b)} \in (0,1)$ and reset/context gates $g_t^{(b)} \in (0,1)^k$ using norm-aware invariants:
   $$s_t^{(b)} = \left[\, \mathrm{Re}\!\left(\overline{h_{t-1}^{(b)}} \star \tilde{x}_t^{(b)}\right),\; \left\|h_{t-1}^{(b)}\right\|_2,\; \left\|\tilde{x}_t^{(b)}\right\|_2 \,\right]$$
   $$z_t^{(b)} = \sigma\!\left(W_z s_t^{(b)} + b_z^{(b)}\right)$$

2. **Unit Rotor Candidate via Exponential / Cayley Map:**  
   An input-driven angular velocity $\omega_t^{(b)} \in \mathrm{Im}(\mathbb{A}_k) \cong \mathbb{R}^{k-1}$ generates a unit rotor $q_t^{(b)} \in S^{k-1}$:
   $$q_t^{(b)} = \exp_{\mathbb{A}_k}\!\left(\omega_t^{(b)}\right) = \cos\!\left(\|\omega_t^{(b)}\|_2\right) e_0 + \frac{\sin\!\left(\|\omega_t^{(b)}\|_2\right)}{\|\omega_t^{(b)}\|_2 + \epsilon} \omega_t^{(b)}$$
   ensuring $\|q_t^{(b)}\|_2 \equiv 1$ for all parameter values without expensive matrix SVD or Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization.

3. **Non-Associative Associator Context Modulation ($k=8$):**  
   When $k=8$, sequential composition of three states $(q_t^{(b)}, u_{t-1}^{(b)}, c_t^{(b)})$ where $c_t^{(b)}$ is a normalized context fiber generates a non-zero **octonionic associator**:
   $$\left[q_t^{(b)}, u_{t-1}^{(b)}, c_t^{(b)}\right] = \left(q_t^{(b)} \star u_{t-1}^{(b)}\right) \star c_t^{(b)} - q_t^{(b)} \star \left(u_{t-1}^{(b)} \star c_t^{(b)}\right)$$
   The associator vanishes identically whenever any two arguments lie in the same quaternionic subalgebra (by Artin's Theorem), acting as a geometric detector of **three-way cross-subalgebra novelty**. We incorporate a gated Moufang-consistent rotor update:
   $$\tilde{u}_t^{(b)} = \mathcal{N}\!\left(q_t^{(b)} \star u_{t-1}^{(b)} + \alpha_t^{(b)} \left[q_t^{(b)}, u_{t-1}^{(b)}, c_t^{(b)}\right]\right)$$
   where $\mathcal{N}(v) = v / \|v\|_2$ projects onto $S^7$.

4. **Geodesic Spherical-Radial State Update:**  
   Finally, the unit phase rotor $u_t^{(b)}$ and radial magnitude $r_t^{(b)}$ are updated via spherical interpolation and leaky radial gating:
   $$u_t^{(b)} = \mathcal{N}\!\left((1 - z_t^{(b)}) u_{t-1}^{(b)} + z_t^{(b)} \tilde{u}_t^{(b)}\right)$$
   $$r_t^{(b)} = (1 - \gamma_t^{(b)}) r_{t-1}^{(b)} + \gamma_t^{(b)} \tilde{r}_t^{(b)}, \qquad h_t^{(b)} = r_t^{(b)} u_t^{(b)}$$

---

## 3. Theoretical Guarantees: Jacobian Spectrum and Parameter Efficiency

### Theorem 1 (Isometric Phase Transport & Bounded Radial Jacobian)
*Let $h_t^{(b)} = r_t^{(b)} u_t^{(b)} \in \mathbb{A}_k$ evolve under the HRU transition with $z_t^{(b)} = 1$ and $\alpha_t^{(b)} = 0$ (pure Hurwitz rotor regime). For any $k \in \{1, 2, 4, 8\}$, the left multiplication operator $L_{q_t^{(b)}}(u) = q_t^{(b)} \star u$ satisfies:*
$$L_{q_t^{(b)}}^\top L_{q_t^{(b)}} = \|q_t^{(b)}\|_2^2 \, I_k = I_k$$
*Consequently, all $k$ singular values of the angular state transition Jacobian $\frac{\partial u_t^{(b)}}{\partial u_{t-1}^{(b)}}$ equal $1$, preventing exponential gradient decay or explosion over arbitrary horizons $T \to \infty$.*

*Proof Sketch:* By the polarized Hurwitz identity, $\langle q \star u, q \star v \rangle = \|q\|_2^2 \langle u, v \rangle$ for all $q, u, v \in \mathbb{A}_k$. Setting $\|q_t^{(b)}\|_2 = 1$ yields $\langle L_q u, L_q v \rangle = \langle u, v \rangle$, so $L_{q_t^{(b)}} \in \mathrm{SO}(k)$ is orthogonal for every $k \in \{1, 2, 4, 8\}$ despite the non-associativity of $\mathbb{O}$ at $k=8$. Notice that while $L_p L_q \neq L_{p \star q}$ in $\mathbb{O}$, the composite operator $L_{q_T} L_{q_{T-1}} \cdots L_{q_1}$ is a product of orthogonal matrices in $\mathrm{SO}(8)$ and therefore remains strictly orthogonal! $\square$

### Proposition 1 (Hamilton / Octonion Parameter Compression)
A dense linear layer mapping $\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ requires $d^2$ real parameters. A Hurwitz-structured linear layer mapping $\mathbb{A}_k^{d/k} \to \mathbb{A}_k^{d/k}$ parameterizes each $k \times k$ block by a single element of $\mathbb{A}_k$ ($k$ real parameters), requiring only:
$$N_{\text{params}}(\mathbb{A}_k) = k \cdot \left(\frac{d}{k}\right)^2 = \frac{d^2}{k}$$
real parameters—achieving a $4\times$ reduction for quaternionic HRU ($k=4$) and an $8\times$ reduction for octonionic HRU ($k=8$) while maintaining full cross-channel coupling within each $k$-dimensional fiber via the Fano multiplication tensor.

---

## 4. Comparative Summary Across the Cayley-Dickson Hierarchy

| Algebra $\mathbb{A}_k$ | Dim $k$ | Commutative | Associative | Alternative | Norm Multiplicative ($\|x\star y\|=\|x\|\|y\|$) | Zero Divisors | Parameter Cost (vs Dense) | Primary Inductive Bias |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Reals ($\mathbb{R}$)** | $1$ | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | None | $1.0\times$ | Independent scalar accumulation |
| **Complex ($\mathbb{C}$)** | $2$ | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | None | $0.5\times$ | Planar $U(1)$ Fourier phase rotation |
| **Quaternions ($\mathbb{H}$)** | $4$ | **No** | Yes | Yes | Yes | None | $0.25\times$ | 3D/4D $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ non-commutative spinor routing |
| **Octonions ($\mathbb{O}$)** | $8$ | **No** | **No** | Yes | Yes | None | $0.125\times$ | Fano-plane 7-triad non-associative context binding |
| *Sedenions ($\mathbb{S}$)* | *16* | *No* | *No* | *No* | ***Fails*** | ***Yes*** | *$0.0625\times$* | *Degenerate null-cones (gradient collapse)* |

---

## 5. Experimental Synthesis & Empirical Findings

Across controlled synthetic and sequence-modeling benchmarks, the HRU family exhibits three consistent empirical signatures:

1. **Long-Horizon Phase & Norm Conservation ($T \ge 1000$):**  
   In synthetic multi-frequency rotational memory tasks and delayed copy/associative recall benchmarks, standard Euclidean GRUs exhibit Jacobian singular value drift ($\sigma_{\min} \to 10^{-6}$), whereas HRU ($k \in \{4, 8\}$) maintains unit angular Jacobian singular values ($\sigma_i \approx 1.000 \pm 10^{-4}$) throughout training, converging in $3.2\times$ fewer epochs.
2. **Sensitivity to Non-Commutative & Non-Associative Parenthesization:**  
   On algebraic word-problem tasks requiring distinction between $(a \cdot b) \cdot c$ and $a \cdot (b \cdot c)$ (hierarchical tree sensitivity without explicit tree supervision), associative models ($k \in \{1, 2, 4\}$) require deep multi-layer nonlinear mixing to break associativity, whereas a single-layer Octonionic HRU ($k=8$) with Fano-Triad Associator gating directly separates parenthesizations via $[a,b,c] \neq 0$, improving hierarchical bracket disambiguation accuracy by $+14.8\%$.

    where a, b, c, d are 8D octonions and * is octonion conjugation.
    """
    a, b = x[..., :8], x[..., 8:]
    c, d = y[..., :8], y[..., 8:]
    d_conj = oct_conjugate(d)
    c_conj = oct_conjugate(c)
    
    first = oct_mul_tensor(a, c) - oct_mul_tensor(d_conj, b)
    second = oct_mul_tensor(d, a) + oct_mul_tensor(b, c_conj)
    return torch.cat([first, second], dim=-1)

if TRITON_AVAILABLE:
    @triton.jit
    def fano_octonion_mul_kernel(
        x_ptr, y_ptr, out_ptr, n_blocks, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr
    ):
        pid = tl.program_id(0)
        offs = pid * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
        mask = offs < n_blocks
        base = offs * 8
        x0 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 0, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x1 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 1, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x2 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 2, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x3 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 3, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x4 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 4, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x5 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 5, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x6 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 6, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        x7 = tl.load(x_ptr + base + 7, mask=mask, other=0.0)

        y0 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 0, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y1 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 1, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y2 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 2, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y3 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 3, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y4 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 4, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y5 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 5, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y6 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 6, mask=mask, other=0.0)
        y7 = tl.load(y_ptr + base + 7, mask=mask, other=0.0)

        z0 = x0*y0 - x1*y1 - x2*y2 - x3*y3 - x4*y4 - x5*y5 - x6*y6 - x7*y7
        z1 = x0*y1 + x1*y0 + x2*y4 + x3*y7 - x4*y2 + x5*y6 - x6*y5 - x7*y3
        z2 = x0*y2 - x1*y4 + x2*y0 + x3*y5 + x4*y1 - x5*y3 + x6*y7 - x7*y6
        z3 = x0*y3 - x1*y7 - x2*y5 + x3*y0 + x4*y6 + x5*y2 - x6*y4 + x7*y1
        z4 = x0*y4 + x1*y2 - x2*y1 - x3*y6 + x4*y0 + x5*y7 + x6*y3 - x7*y5
        z5 = x0*y5 - x1*y6 + x2*y3 - x3*y2 - x4*y7 + x5*y0 + x6*y1 + x7*y4
        z6 = x0*y6 + x1*y5 - x2*y7 + x3*y4 - x4*y3 - x5*y1 + x6*y0 + x7*y2
        z7 = x0*y7 + x1*y3 + x2*y6 - x3*y1 + x4*y5 - x5*y4 - x6*y2 + x7*y0

        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 0, z0, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 1, z1, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 2, z2, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 3, z3, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 4, z4, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 5, z5, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 6, z6, mask=mask)
        tl.store(out_ptr + base + 7, z7, mask=mask)

class RealPyTorchOctonionCell(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, n_fibers: int = 8):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_fibers = n_fibers
        self.register_buffer("basis_tensor", OCT_TENSOR)
        # Unit rotor parameter per fiber (in S^7)
        self.w_rotor = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(n_fibers, 8) * 0.1 + torch.tensor([1.0] + [0.0]*7))
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.full((1, n_fibers, 1), 0.2))
        self.gate_w = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, n_fibers, 1))

    def forward(self, u_t: torch.Tensor, h_prev: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        u_t: (B, C, 8) normalized input
        h_prev: (B, C, 8) normalized state on S^7
        """
        w_unit = F.normalize(self.w_rotor, p=2, dim=-1).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, C, 8)
        # wh = w * h
        wh = oct_mul_tensor(w_unit, h_prev, self.basis_tensor)
        # wh_u = (w * h) * u
        wh_u = oct_mul_tensor(wh, u_t, self.basis_tensor)
        # hu = h * u
        hu = oct_mul_tensor(h_prev, u_t, self.basis_tensor)
        # w_hu = w * (h * u)
        w_hu = oct_mul_tensor(w_unit, hu, self.basis_tensor)
        # Fano-Triad associator
        assoc = wh_u - w_hu
        cand = F.normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * assoc, p=2, dim=-1)
        z = torch.sigmoid(self.gate_w)
        # Geodesic spherical projection onto S^7
        h_next = F.normalize((1.0 - z) * h_prev + z * cand, p=2, dim=-1)
        return h_next


class PyTorchHRU_LM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int = 64, with_skips: bool = False):
        super().__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_fibers = d_model // 8
        self.with_skips = with_skips

        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.cell = RealPyTorchOctonionCell(self.n_fibers)
        # Multi-scale readout from hidden state + input representation
        self.fc_out = nn.Linear(d_model * 2, vocab_size)

        if with_skips:
            # Paper's hidden tables
            self.W_ctx1 = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, vocab_size)
            self.W_ctx2 = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, vocab_size)
            nn.init.zeros_(self.W_ctx1.weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(self.W_ctx2.weight)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, L = x.shape
        emb = self.embedding(x)  # (B, L, D)
        u_seq = F.normalize(emb.view(B, L, self.n_fibers, 8), p=2, dim=-1)

        h = torch.zeros(B, self.n_fibers, 8, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        h[:, :, 0] = 1.0  # Identity element on S^7

        h_list = []
        for t in range(L):
            h = self.cell(u_seq[:, t], h)
            h_list.append(h)

        h_seq = torch.stack(h_list, dim=1).view(B, L, self.d_model)
        feats = torch.cat([h_seq, emb], dim=-1)
        logits = self.fc_out(feats)

        if self.with_skips:
            x_prev = torch.roll(x, shifts=1, dims=1)
            x_prev[:, 0] = 0
            logits = logits + self.W_ctx1(x) + self.W_ctx2(x_prev)

        return logits


class PyTorchPureSkipsOnly_LM(nn.Module):
    """Zero recurrence model: only W_ctx1 (bigram) + W_ctx2 (trigram) + bias"""
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int):
        super().__init__()
        self.W_ctx1 = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, vocab_size)
        self.W_ctx2 = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, vocab_size)
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(vocab_size))

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x_prev = torch.roll(x, shifts=1, dims=1)
        x_prev[:, 0] = 0
        return self.W_ctx1(x) + self.W_ctx2(x_prev) + self.bias


class PyTorchRNN_LM(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, d_model: int, rnn_type: str = "LSTM"):
        super().__init__()
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        if rnn_type == "LSTM":
            self.rnn = nn.LSTM(d_model, d_model, batch_first=True)
        else:
            self.rnn = nn.GRU(d_model, d_model, batch_first=True)
        self.fc_out = nn.Linear(d_model * 2, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        emb = self.embedding(x)
        out, _ = self.rnn(emb)
        feats = torch.cat([out, emb], dim=-1)
        return self.fc_out(feats)


def run_fair_lm_benchmark(steps: int = 300, seq_len: int = 64, batch_size: int = 32) -> dict:
    text = load_corpus()
    chars = sorted(list(set(text)))
    vocab_size = len(chars)
    stoi = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(chars)}
    encoded = np.array([stoi[c] for c in text], dtype=np.int64)

    split = int(0.9 * len(encoded))
    train_data = encoded[:split]
    val_data = encoded[split:]

    def get_batch(data):
        starts = np.random.randint(0, len(data) - seq_len - 1, size=batch_size)
        x = np.stack([data[s:s+seq_len] for s in starts])
        y = np.stack([data[s+1:s+seq_len+1] for s in starts])
        return torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.long, device=DEVICE), torch.tensor(y, dtype=torch.long, device=DEVICE)

    models_to_test = {
        "Paper_HRU_with_skips (Hidden Tables)": PyTorchHRU_LM(vocab_size, d_model=64, with_skips=True).to(DEVICE),
        "Pure_HRU_d64 (No Skips)": PyTorchHRU_LM(vocab_size, d_model=64, with_skips=False).to(DEVICE),
        "Pure_Skips_Only (0 Recurrent Params)": PyTorchPureSkipsOnly_LM(vocab_size).to(DEVICE),
        "PyTorch_LSTM (Matched ~13k params)": PyTorchRNN_LM(vocab_size, d_model=32, rnn_type="LSTM").to(DEVICE),
        "PyTorch_GRU (Matched ~13k params)": PyTorchRNN_LM(vocab_size, d_model=36, rnn_type="GRU").to(DEVICE),
        "PyTorch_LSTM (Full ~21k params)": PyTorchRNN_LM(vocab_size, d_model=48, rnn_type="LSTM").to(DEVICE),
    }

    results = {}
    print(f"\n{'Model':<40} | {'Params':>8} | {'Val Loss':>8} | {'Val BPC':>8} | {'Val PPL':>8} | {'tok/s':>9}")
    print("-" * 92)

    for name, model in models_to_test.items():
        n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
        opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=3e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)
        
        # Training loop
        t0 = time.time()
        model.train()
        for step in range(steps):
            xb, yb = get_batch(train_data)
            opt.zero_grad()
            logits = model(xb)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.view(-1, vocab_size), yb.view(-1))
            loss.backward()
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0)
            opt.step()

        elapsed = time.time() - t0
        tps = (steps * batch_size * seq_len) / max(elapsed, 1e-5)

        # Validation
        model.eval()
        val_losses = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(20):
                xv, yv = get_batch(val_data)
                v_logits = model(xv)
                v_loss = F.cross_entropy(v_logits.view(-1, vocab_size), yv.view(-1))
                val_losses.append(v_loss.item())

        mean_v_loss = float(np.mean(val_losses))
        val_bpc = mean_v_loss / math.log(2.0)
        val_ppl = math.exp(min(mean_v_loss, 20.0))

        print(f"{name:<40} | {n_params:>8,d} | {mean_v_loss:>8.4f} | {val_bpc:>8.3f} | {val_ppl:>8.2f} | {tps:>9,.0f}")
        results[name] = {
            "parameters": n_params,
            "val_loss": mean_v_loss,
            "val_bpc": val_bpc,
            "val_ppl": val_ppl,
            "tokens_per_sec": tps
        }

    return results

# PHASE 3 [TEST 2]: GRADIENT FLOW & LYAPUNOV SPECTRUM ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================
def test_gradient_flow_and_lyapunov() -> dict:
    """
    Measures ||dh_L / dh_0|| and effective Lyapunov exponent 1/L * ln(||dh_L / dh_0||)
    across sequence lengths L in [32, 64, 128, 256, 512].
    """
    lengths = [32, 64, 128, 256, 512]
    d_model = 8  # 1 fiber for Octonion (8D), 16D for Sedenion
    results = {
        "lengths": lengths,
        "pure_octonion_ungated": [],
        "octonion_hru_geodesic_gated": [],
        "sedenion_zero_divisor_aligned": [],
        "vanilla_tanh_rnn": [],
        "lstm": []
    }

    tensor = OCT_TENSOR.to(DEVICE)

    for L in lengths:
        # 1. Pure Octonion Ungated Rotor: h_t = (w_t * h_{t-1}) / ||w_t||
        h0_oct = torch.randn(1, 1, 8, device=DEVICE, requires_grad=True)
        h = F.normalize(h0_oct, p=2, dim=-1)
        w_seq = F.normalize(torch.randn(L, 1, 8, device=DEVICE), p=2, dim=-1)
        for t in range(L):
            h = oct_mul_tensor(w_seq[t], h, tensor)
            # By Hurwitz theorem, ||w*h|| = ||w|| ||h|| = 1 without renormalization
        loss = h.sum()
        grad_h0 = torch.autograd.grad(loss, h0_oct)[0]
        norm_ratio = torch.norm(grad_h0).item()
        lyap = math.log(max(norm_ratio, 1e-15)) / L
        results["pure_octonion_ungated"].append({"ratio": norm_ratio, "lyapunov": lyap})

        # 2. Octonion HRU Geodesic Gated: h_t = normalize((1-z)*h_{t-1} + z*cand)
        h0_gated = torch.randn(1, 1, 8, device=DEVICE, requires_grad=True)
        h = F.normalize(h0_gated, p=2, dim=-1)
        z = torch.tensor([[[0.5]]], device=DEVICE)
        for t in range(L):
            cand = oct_mul_tensor(w_seq[t], h, tensor)
            h = F.normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand, p=2, dim=-1)
        loss = h.sum()
        grad_h0 = torch.autograd.grad(loss, h0_gated)[0]
        norm_ratio = torch.norm(grad_h0).item()
        lyap = math.log(max(norm_ratio, 1e-15)) / L
        results["octonion_hru_geodesic_gated"].append({"ratio": norm_ratio, "lyapunov": lyap})

        # 3. Sedenion (16D) aligned near zero-divisor subspace
        # Zero divisor example: x = (e_1 + e_10), y = (e_4 - e_15)
        # In 16D: e_1 = index 1, e_10 = index 10.
        h0_sed = torch.randn(1, 1, 16, device=DEVICE, requires_grad=True)
        h = F.normalize(h0_sed, p=2, dim=-1)
        w_sed = torch.zeros(1, 1, 16, device=DEVICE)
        w_sed[0, 0, 1] = 1.0
        w_sed[0, 0, 10] = 1.0  # (e_1 + e_10)
        w_sed = F.normalize(w_sed, p=2, dim=-1)
        
        # Perturb slightly to avoid exact 0 in forward while testing gradient collapse
        eps_noise = torch.randn(1, 1, 16, device=DEVICE) * 0.05
        w_sed_perturbed = F.normalize(w_sed + eps_noise, p=2, dim=-1)

        for t in range(min(L, 64)):  # Keep small to avoid complete underflow
            h = sedenion_mul(w_sed_perturbed, h)
            h = F.normalize(h + 1e-8, p=2, dim=-1)
        loss = h.sum()
        try:
            grad_h0 = torch.autograd.grad(loss, h0_sed, allow_unused=True)[0]
            norm_ratio = torch.norm(grad_h0).item() if grad_h0 is not None else 0.0
        except Exception:
            norm_ratio = 0.0
        lyap = math.log(max(norm_ratio, 1e-15)) / min(L, 64)
        results["sedenion_zero_divisor_aligned"].append({"ratio": norm_ratio, "lyapunov": lyap})

        # 4. Vanilla tanh RNN: h_t = tanh(W h_{t-1})
        h0_tanh = torch.randn(1, 8, device=DEVICE, requires_grad=True)
        h = h0_tanh
        W_tanh = torch.randn(8, 8, device=DEVICE) * 1.0
        for t in range(L):
            h = torch.tanh(h @ W_tanh)
        loss = h.sum()
        grad_h0 = torch.autograd.grad(loss, h0_tanh)[0]
        norm_ratio = torch.norm(grad_h0).item()
        lyap = math.log(max(norm_ratio, 1e-15)) / L
        results["vanilla_tanh_rnn"].append({"ratio": norm_ratio, "lyapunov": lyap})

        # 5. nn.LSTM
        lstm = nn.LSTM(8, 8, batch_first=True).to(DEVICE)
        h0_c = (torch.randn(1, 1, 8, device=DEVICE, requires_grad=True),
                torch.randn(1, 1, 8, device=DEVICE))
        x_in = torch.randn(1, L, 8, device=DEVICE)
        out, _ = lstm(x_in, h0_c)
        loss = out.sum()
        grad_h0 = torch.autograd.grad(loss, h0_c[0])[0]
        norm_ratio = torch.norm(grad_h0).item()
        lyap = math.log(max(norm_ratio, 1e-15)) / L
        results["lstm"].append({"ratio": norm_ratio, "lyapunov": lyap})

    print("\n--- TEST 2: Gradient Flow Ratio ||dh_L / dh_0|| & Lyapunov Exponent ---")
    print(f"{'Length L':<10} | {'Pure Oct Ungated':<18} | {'HRU Geodesic Gated':<18} | {'Sedenion Zero-Div':<18} | {'Vanilla Tanh RNN':<18}")
    print("-" * 90)
    for i, L in enumerate(lengths):
        po = f"{results['pure_octonion_ungated'][i]['ratio']:.3e} (λ={results['pure_octonion_ungated'][i]['lyapunov']:.2f})"

    norm_xy_oct = torch.norm(xy_oct, dim=-1)
    norm_x_norm_y = torch.norm(x_oct, dim=-1) * torch.norm(y_oct, dim=-1)
    oct_norm_err = torch.max(torch.abs(norm_xy_oct - norm_x_norm_y)).item()

    # 2. Sedenion Norm Composition: Does ||x * y|| == ||x|| * ||y|| hold?
    x_sed = torch.randn(100, 16)
    y_sed = torch.randn(100, 16)
    xy_sed = sedenion_mul(x_sed, y_sed)
    norm_xy_sed = torch.norm(xy_sed, dim=-1)
    norm_x_norm_y_sed = torch.norm(x_sed, dim=-1) * torch.norm(y_sed, dim=-1)

    zd_x[10] = 1.0

    zd_y = torch.zeros(16)
    zd_y[4] = 1.0
    zd_y[15] = -1.0

    product_zd = sedenion_mul(zd_x.unsqueeze(0), zd_y.unsqueeze(0)).squeeze(0)

def get_cayley_dickson_tensor(dim: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Constructs the canonical Cayley-Dickson multiplication tensor T of shape
    (dim, dim, dim) such that (e_i * e_j) = sum_k T[i, j, k] * e_k.
    Guaranteed dtype=torch.float32 to prevent long/float mismatch.
    """
    assert dim in (1, 2, 4, 8, 16), f"Unsupported Cayley-Dickson dimension: {dim}"
    if dim == 1:
        return torch.ones((1, 1, 1), dtype=torch.float32)

    sub_dim = dim // 2
    sub_T = get_cayley_dickson_tensor(sub_dim)  # (sub_dim, sub_dim, sub_dim)
    T = torch.zeros((dim, dim, dim), dtype=torch.float32)

    # (a, b)(c, d) = (ac - bar(d)b, da + b bar(c))
    # where bar(e_0) = e_0, bar(e_k) = -e_k for k > 0
    # Block 1: e_i * e_j (i < sub, j < sub)
    T[:sub_dim, :sub_dim, :sub_dim] = sub_T

    # Block 2: e_i * e_{l + sub} -> (0, e_l * e_i)
    for i in range(sub_dim):
        for l in range(sub_dim):
            T[i, l + sub_dim, sub_dim:] = sub_T[l, i, :]

    # Block 3: e_{k + sub} * e_j -> (0, e_k * bar(e_j))
    for k in range(sub_dim):
        for j in range(sub_dim):
            sign = 1.0 if j == 0 else -1.0
            T[k + sub_dim, j, sub_dim:] = sign * sub_T[k, j, :]

    # Block 4: e_{k + sub} * e_{l + sub} -> (-bar(e_l) * e_k, 0)
    for k in range(sub_dim):
        for l in range(sub_dim):
            sign = -1.0 if l == 0 else 1.0
            T[k + sub_dim, l + sub_dim, :sub_dim] = sign * sub_T[l, k, :]

    return T

    if x.dtype != torch.float32:
        x = x.to(dtype=torch.float32)
    if y.dtype != torch.float32:
        y = y.to(dtype=torch.float32)
    T = T.to(dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
    return torch.einsum("...i,...j,ijk->...k", x, y, T)


def cd_mul_tensor(x: torch.Tensor, y: torch.Tensor, dim: int = 8) -> torch.Tensor:
    """General Cayley-Dickson multiplication for dim in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}."""
    T = CD_TENSORS[dim].to(dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
    if x.dtype != torch.float32:
        x = x.to(dtype=torch.float32)
    if y.dtype != torch.float32:
        y = y.to(dtype=torch.float32)
    return torch.einsum("...i,...j,ijk->...k", x, y, T)


def oct_associator_tensor(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor, c: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Computes non-associative associator [a, b, c] = (a * b) * c - a * (b * c)."""
    ab = oct_mul_tensor(a, b)
    ab_c = oct_mul_tensor(ab, c)
    bc = oct_mul_tensor(b, c)
    a_bc = oct_mul_tensor(a, bc)
    return ab_c - a_bc

def load_verified_shakespeare(cache_dir: str = ".") -> str:
    path = os.path.join(cache_dir, "tinyshakespeare.txt")
    text = ""
    if os.path.exists(path) and os.path.getsize(path) == 1115394:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            text = f.read()
    else:
        # Search sibling / parent directory
        for alt in ["tinyshakespeare.txt", "../tinyshakespeare.txt", "/kaggle/input/tinyshakespeare/input.txt"]:
            if os.path.exists(alt) and os.path.getsize(alt) == 1115394:
                with open(alt, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    text = f.read()
                    break

    if not text:
        try:
            req = urllib.request.Request(SHAKESPEARE_URL, headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0"})
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
                text = resp.read().decode("utf-8")
                with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(text)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[Warning] Network fetch failed: {e}")

    # TEST 0 ASSERTIONS
    assert len(text) == 1115394, f"Corpus length must be exactly 1,115,394 chars, got {len(text)}"

    assert "First Citizen:" in text, "Corpus corrupted: missing 'First Citizen:'"
    assert text[:1000] not in text[1000:], "Corpus corrupted: loop/fallback artifact detected"
    return text


class CharTokenizer:
    def __init__(self, text: str):
        self.chars = sorted(list(set(text)))
        self.vocab_size = len(self.chars)
        self.stoi = {ch: i for i, ch in enumerate(self.chars)}
        self.itos = {i: ch for i, ch in enumerate(self.chars)}

    def encode(self, s: str) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.tensor([self.stoi[c] for c in s], dtype=torch.long)

    def decode(self, ids: List[int]) -> str:
        return "".join([self.itos[int(i)] for i in ids])

# 2. PYTORCH MODEL IMPLEMENTATIONS WITH FULL AUTOGRAD
# ============================================================================
class HRULanguageModel(nn.Module):
    """
    Full PyTorch HRU Language Model with true backpropagation through time.
    Supports k in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}, ablation of alpha, and pure rotor z=1.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_size: int = 65,
        d_model: int = 64,
        k: int = 8,
        use_alpha: bool = True,
        force_pure_rotor: bool = False,
        use_hurwitz_compression: bool = False,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % k == 0
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.k = k
        self.n_fibers = d_model // k
        self.use_alpha = use_alpha and (k == 8)
        self.force_pure_rotor = force_pure_rotor
        self.use_hurwitz_compression = use_hurwitz_compression

        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)

        if use_hurwitz_compression and k == 8:
            # 8:1 parameter compression: (n_fibers, n_fibers, 8)
            self.W_hurwitz = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(self.n_fibers, self.n_fibers, 8) * 0.1)
            self.in_proj = None
        else:
            self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)
            self.W_hurwitz = None

        # Unit rotor per fiber
        self.w_rotor = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(self.n_fibers, k) * 0.2)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.w_rotor[:, 0] += 0.8

        if self.use_alpha:
            self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.full((1, self.n_fibers, 1), 0.15))
        else:
            self.alpha = None

        if not force_pure_rotor:
            self.gate_proj = nn.Linear(d_model * 2, self.n_fibers)
        else:
            self.gate_proj = None

        self.readout = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)

    def _project_input(self, x_emb: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        B, L, _ = x_emb.shape
        if self.use_hurwitz_compression and self.k == 8:
            # Block-octonion linear map
            x_fib = x_emb.view(B, L, self.n_fibers, 1, 8)
            W_fib = self.W_hurwitz.view(1, 1, self.n_fibers, self.n_fibers, 8)
            out = oct_mul_tensor(x_fib, W_fib).sum(dim=2)  # (B, L, n_fibers, 8)
            return out.view(B, L, self.d_model)
        else:
            return self.in_proj(x_emb)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, return_h_seq: bool = False):
        B, L = input_ids.shape
        x_emb = self.emb(input_ids)
        u_proj = self._project_input(x_emb).view(B, L, self.n_fibers, self.k)
        u_norm = F.normalize(u_proj, p=2, dim=-1)

        w_unit = F.normalize(self.w_rotor, p=2, dim=-1).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, n_fibers, k)

        h = torch.zeros(B, self.n_fibers, self.k, device=input_ids.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        h[:, :, 0] = 1.0

        h_seq = []
        for t in range(L):
            u_t = u_norm[:, t]  # (B, n_fibers, k)
            if self.k == 8:
                wh = oct_mul_tensor(w_unit, h)
                wh_u = oct_mul_tensor(wh, u_t)
                if self.use_alpha:
                    hu = oct_mul_tensor(h, u_t)
                    w_hu = oct_mul_tensor(w_unit, hu)
                    assoc = wh_u - w_hu
                    cand = F.normalize(wh_u + self.alpha * assoc, p=2, dim=-1)
                else:
                    cand = F.normalize(wh_u, p=2, dim=-1)
            else:
                wh = cd_mul_tensor(w_unit, h, dim=self.k)
                cand = F.normalize(cd_mul_tensor(wh, u_t, dim=self.k), p=2, dim=-1)

            if self.force_pure_rotor:
                h = cand
            else:
                flat_h = h.view(B, -1)
                flat_u = u_proj[:, t].view(B, -1)
                z = torch.sigmoid(self.gate_proj(torch.cat([flat_u, flat_h], dim=-1))).unsqueeze(-1)
                h = F.normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand, p=2, dim=-1)

            h_seq.append(h.view(B, self.d_model))

        h_stack = torch.stack(h_seq, dim=1)  # (B, L, d_model)
        logits = self.readout(h_stack)
        if return_h_seq:
            return logits, h_stack
        return logits


class SO8OrthogonalBlockRNN(nn.Module):
    """Control model: Block-diagonal SO(8) orthogonal rotations without Octonion algebra."""
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = 65, d_model: int = 64):
        super().__init__()
        assert d_model % 8 == 0
        self.vocab_size = vocab_size
        self.d_model = d_model
        self.n_fibers = d_model // 8
        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model, bias=False)

        # Skew-symmetric generators for SO(8): A = -A^T -> exp(A) in SO(8)
        self.skew_params = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(self.n_fibers, 8, 8) * 0.1)
        self.gate_proj = nn.Linear(d_model * 2, self.n_fibers)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)

    def _get_rotation_matrices(self) -> torch.Tensor:
        A = self.skew_params - self.skew_params.transpose(-1, -2)
        return torch.matrix_exp(A)  # (n_fibers, 8, 8)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor):
        B, L = input_ids.shape
        x_emb = self.emb(input_ids)
        u_proj = self.in_proj(x_emb).view(B, L, self.n_fibers, 8)
        R = self._get_rotation_matrices()  # (n_fibers, 8, 8)

        h = torch.zeros(B, self.n_fibers, 8, device=input_ids.device, dtype=torch.float32)
        h[:, :, 0] = 1.0
        h_seq = []
        for t in range(L):
            u_t = u_proj[:, t]
            # Orthogonal rotation per fiber
            Rh = torch.einsum("fij,bfj->bfi", R, h)
            cand = F.normalize(Rh + u_t, p=2, dim=-1)
            flat_h = h.view(B, -1)
            flat_u = u_t.view(B, -1)
            z = torch.sigmoid(self.gate_proj(torch.cat([flat_u, flat_h], dim=-1))).unsqueeze(-1)
            h = F.normalize((1.0 - z) * h + z * cand, p=2, dim=-1)
            h_seq.append(h.view(B, self.d_model))

        h_stack = torch.stack(h_seq, dim=1)
        return self.readout(h_stack)


class LSTMLanguageModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = 65, d_emb: int = 48, d_h: int = 44):
        super().__init__()
        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_emb)
        self.lstm = nn.LSTM(d_emb, d_h, batch_first=True)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(d_h, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor):
        x = self.emb(input_ids)
        out, _ = self.lstm(x)
        return self.readout(out)


class GRULanguageModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = 65, d_emb: int = 48, d_h: int = 50):
        super().__init__()
        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_emb)
        self.gru = nn.GRU(d_emb, d_h, batch_first=True)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(d_h, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor):
        x = self.emb(input_ids)
        out, _ = self.gru(x)
        return self.readout(out)


class NoRecurrenceControl(nn.Module):
    """Embedding + direct linear readout baseline."""
    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int = 65, d_model: int = 64):
        super().__init__()
        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.readout = nn.Linear(d_model, vocab_size)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor):
        return self.readout(self.emb(input_ids))
